page: Amazon Web Services r5n.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical execution core with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio that characterizes the R5 family. There is no bundled local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent filesystem operations, and it features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements place the r5n.large primarily in lower-tier performance segments due to its compact dual-vCPU footprint. In CPU testing, it achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 1105.0 and a multi-core score of 1312.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1997.67, both falling into bottom-percentile brackets. Memory benchmarks show large-block uncached read and write throughput of 13.58 GB/sec and 11.69 GB/sec, respectively. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET throughput reached 1.66 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measured 1.84 GB/sec.

The r5n.large is engineered for memory-dependent entry workloads requiring stable RAM density and network integration without excessive compute overhead. It is well-matched for intermediate caching tiers, smaller Redis key-value stores, memory-resident microservices, and modest relational database replicas that operate within its 16 GB memory envelope.
